public.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
public.description: Given a valid binary search tree with distinct values, return its kth smallest value, with k starting at 1. k is valid and the tree is nonempty. Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: the first value is the root; each non-null node consumes the next two entries as left and right children. Null marks a missing child; trailing nulls may be omitted. Empty arrays mean no tree. Values are integers from -10000 to 10000, with at most 200 nodes.
hints: Inorder traversal of a BST visits values in ascending order.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and solutions, 2026. Adapted from a standard algorithmic problem; no third-party exercise text used.

explanation: Count nodes during left-root-right traversal and retain the kth value. O(n) time, O(height) recursion space.
